speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand your infant has been vomiting bile and cannot pass meconium. To determine the cause, can you tell me how old the baby is and when the vomiting started?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-day-old male infant. The infant was born via a home birth without complications. The mother reports that the infant has had bilious vomiting and has not been able to pass meconium since birth. She also notes that the infant's abdomen appears distended.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Hirschsprung Disease (Congenital Aganglionic Megacolon).

The clinical presentation of bilious vomiting, failure to pass meconium within 48 hours of birth, and abdominal distension in a 2-day-old male is highly specific for Hirschsprung disease. While intestinal atresia and volvulus are differential considerations, the complete failure to pass meconium strongly favors this diagnosis.
